PullRequest.Title: agentHost: chats with their own harness in a session (multipleChatProviders)

## Summary

Lets one Agents-window session hold chats on different harnesses (agents), for example a Claude chat in a Copilot session.

The feature is behind `chat.agentHost.multipleChatProviders.enabled` (APPLICATION scope, off by default). With the setting off, behaviour, protocol offers and tool descriptions are identical to `main`.

It builds on AHP microsoft/agent-host-protocol#534 (merged; synced at `5872a476`).

## What's included

- **Per-chat agent:** create, route and persist a chat's agent in the `agent-host.db` metadata (`chatAgentProvider:<chat>`). Downgrade-safe.
- **Per-chat config model:** each chat has its own `chatMutable` values. A chat on another agent has its own schema. The main chat follows the session pickers.
- **Harness picker** in the new-chat and nested-session composers.
- **Per-chat model and mode pickers.**
- **Cross-agent moves**, also requiring `chat.agentHost.moveChats.enabled`.
- **`chat/moved`.**
- **Safety for older clients:** config keys are validated against the chat's agent, and foreign models are ignored.
- **`create_session` `harness`** for agent-to-agent work.
- **Turning the setting on without a reload:** the local host gets the setting when it is spawned.
- **F1 fixes:**
  - No subscription fan-out: the response file-changes provider no longer subscribes every chat in a session's catalog.
  - A subscribe dropped by a reconnect is sent again.
  - A subscribe or refresh that resolves after its subscription was released is unsubscribed again.

## Needs real providers (please try)

- A Copilot + Claude session.
- Move to New Session of a Claude chat.
- Per-chat model and auto-approve pickers.
- A side chat of a Claude chat.
- The main chat following the session pickers.

## Known follow-ups / not in this PR

- F3: a chat whose agent is disabled shows "Resource not found".
- B4: Send to New Chat. Under investigation; likely pre-existing.
- Draft tombstones on a harness switch. Under investigation.
- The agent-plugins dev-launch `argv.json` note is pre-existing.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: An observed response-file-changes value with an initially unresolved backend chat created and retained one Agent Host subscription for every chat in the session catalog, including archived chats, instead of subscribing only the response's chat.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Opening or reconnecting a session with many catalog chats caused subscription IPC, host-side subscription state, and chat snapshot work to scale with the full catalog for one response.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: When a response's backend chat is not resolved at request time, the provider now waits for the session snapshot, resolves that exact chat, and maps only a singleton URI rather than every catalog chat.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The deleted base line built a mapped source for every URI in source.chatUris, and each mapping calls _getChatSource(chatUri), which acquires a chat subscription. The added resolver instead derives a singleton URI from the session state. The new test constructs six peer chats plus the default chat and proves the unresolved-after-reconnect path now subscribes only the default chat while preserving the file diff result.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent Host startup, session listing, and restoring sessions containing chats from multiple agents
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first session list now waits for the indexed chat-agent metadata read before returning stamped chat metadata. Restoring a session waits for catalog/chat-row hydration and, only for chats whose agent differs from the session's, that agent's config schema before registration; transcript materialization remains lazy.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Range-scan chatAgentProvider metadata and build the in-memory chat-to-agent map
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One indexed range scan per AgentService lifetime; all callers share the same promise/map, with rows proportional to chats that use a foreign agent rather than all chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-chat agent metadata existed and no corresponding database scan was needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The cold first list/restore waits for this read; warm lists and restores reuse the map.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the foreign agent's chat configuration schema for restored peer chats
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one provider resolveChatConfig call per distinct foreign agent and primary working directory in one session restore; peer chats sharing that key coalesce on one promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All chats used the session agent/schema, so restore did not resolve a second agent's schema.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A foreign-agent chat is not registered until its schema resolves; same-agent chats add no provider call, and histories remain off the restore critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hydrate persisted peer-chat title, draft, and config rows
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One hydration per persisted peer chat, run with Promise.all; this boundary and cardinality predate the change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same peer-chat metadata rows were hydrated before registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session restore already waited for metadata hydration; the diff only layers coalesced foreign-agent schema resolution onto affected chats.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Persisted sessions, peer chats per restored session, and effective distinct foreign agents after grouping; the dominant new database read is one scan over foreign-agent records, not one query per session/chat.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Peer metadata hydrations run concurrently as before. Foreign-agent config resolutions are coalesced by provider plus primary working directory within each restore, while the metadata range scan is globally promise-coalesced and cached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold startup performs one metadata scan; all later callers reuse the mutable cached map. Foreign-agent config caching is scoped to a single session restore because working-directory context can differ. Failures clear the metadata promise so later restores can retry rather than pinning a negative result.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the database cache, restore Promise.all, and per-key config promise cache are directly visible in the changed call path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider config resolution cost varies by agent SDK and workspace, but its grouped cardinality and critical-path placement are explicit. Typical registered-agent counts are small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the new cold work is required to route persisted foreign-agent chats safely, the global database read is coalesced, and provider config calls are grouped by effective agent/workspace cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create a peer chat on another harness, switch its harness in the composer, and send immediately
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Creating the selected draft must complete before it appears. A send during a harness switch explicitly waits for that single switch, then workspace resolution and the normal send path proceed against the replacement chat.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send createChat to Agent Host with the requested provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create request per newly selected harness when no untitled draft for that harness exists; session management reuses an existing matching untitled draft.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Creating a peer chat used the same IPC boundary but always used the session's agent; there was no harness-switch flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Draft creation is on the picker action path, and immediate send waits for the in-flight switch to avoid sending to the deleted draft.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the selected chat-agent metadata before publishing the chat catalog row
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One upsert for a newly created chat whose agent differs from its session's; same-agent chats perform none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-chat agent record was required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The write is intentionally before catalog publication and therefore on foreign-agent chat creation's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Delete the empty draft replaced by a harness switch
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one delete after one successful replacement per picker action; repeated picks cannot overlap because _harnessSwitch admits one operation at a time.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no cross-harness draft replacement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Deletion is awaited by the picker operation, and send waits for that operation; it does not fan out across chats.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve selected-folder/worktree facts after the replacement chat changes agent
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cancellable refresh for the selected folder after a chat replacement; superseding refreshes settle through cancellation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The draft's agent could not change, so this refresh was unnecessary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Send waits for the current refresh so it does not launch with stale workspace choices.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: User harness-picker actions; effective work is constant per action and does not scale with the session's chat count or history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Harness switches are explicitly serialized to one in flight. Folder refreshes cancel/supersede prior resolutions. The create and subsequent delete are sequential, not burst-concurrent.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An existing untitled chat with the requested harness is reused. Provider/session capability and model snapshots are in-memory; no negative cache is added. Folder refresh state is replaced and cancellation-aware.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the create/delete ordering, one-operation guard, reuse condition, and send await are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote Agent Host latency and provider config latency vary, so an individual switch may be perceptible, but multiplicity is bounded by direct user actions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added boundaries are bounded to one user-requested switch, serialized, and required to replace an empty draft safely.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or reconnect a chat and render response file changes, model picker, respondent identity, tabs, and sessions-list labels
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Loading the selected chat waits for its model reference and required Agent Host subscriptions. Respondent/model presentation and accessibility labels use in-memory observables. Response-file changes subscribe to the exact chat after session state resolves.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to Agent Host session/chat state needed by the selected response
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One exact chat subscription for a response when the resolver is available; the diff removes the previous full-catalog subscription fan-out, including archived chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: When the backend chat was unresolved at request time, one logical response could subscribe every chat URI in the session catalog. This PR fixes that shipped regression and it was recorded separately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The exact chat snapshot is needed to show file changes; unrelated chat snapshots no longer block or consume host work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Chats in the active session, visible tab/list rows, and response updates. The fixed subscription cardinality is one exact chat rather than all catalog chats; UI scans are linear over each session's own small chat list and perform no boundary calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable recomputation is synchronous and in-memory. Chat subscriptions remain refcounted/coalesced by resource. Provider model/session-type events share one weakly keyed signal per provider, and only the bound chat's respondent autorun is retained.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-request observables are cached by session/chat/request key; provider-change signals are shared in a WeakMap; model snapshots and harness presentations are in-memory. Subscription errors can retry without permanently poisoning the resource.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed resolver, subscription helper, and regression test establish exact pre/post cardinality.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions can contain many archived chats, making the removed fan-out large; normal UI list sizes and model counts are comparatively small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No new regression; this path contains a concrete boundary-fanout performance fix, while the added presentation work is bounded in-memory UI work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable multiple chat providers at runtime and reconnect an already-running host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: If the host gate is on but the previous handshake did not advertise the capability, the client deliberately closes the transport, performs one fresh initialize, then restores held subscriptions before the connection is usable again.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fresh initialize and replay of active subscriptions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one reinitialize per gate-on period per connection; replay cardinality equals currently held, refcounted subscriptions, not all known sessions/chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no multiple-provider capability negotiation or setting-triggered reinitialize.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The opt-in runtime setting transition briefly moves the connection through reconnecting; local hosts launched with the setting already on avoid this reinitialize via the environment seed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of currently held subscriptions at the moment the user turns the feature on; inactive catalog sessions are not subscribed solely for this transition.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The reinitialize is guarded by _reinitializedForChatProviders and the connection state. Active subscriptions replay through existing subscription management; in-flight subscribe requests retry after reconnection and released resources are unsubscribed again.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The guard resets only when the setting or host gate turns off. The initialize result is observable and reused after connection. Local host startup seeds the setting before the first handshake, avoiding a cold double handshake.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the one-shot guard, transport close, initialize branch, and active-subscription restoration are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Reconnect duration depends on transport and host location; active subscription count varies with visible/open sessions.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the one-time opt-in reconnect is bounded, necessary for protocol negotiation, and avoided on the common local cold-start path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move a chat across agents or archive/unarchive a mixed-agent session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cross-agent moves run through the existing global move sequencer and await catalog/database/config preparation before commit. Archive/unarchive updates session state immediately; worktree cleanup and provider notifications are launched asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/write chat catalog, storage identity, chat-agent metadata, and moved-chat records during a move
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded to the moved chat chain and source/destination sessions; chat-agent deletion/upsert is batched, and moves are globally serialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Moves were limited to sessions of the same agent and did not update per-chat agent/config records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Move completion waits for durable metadata/catalog ordering so restart cannot route the chat to the wrong agent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Notify each distinct agent represented in the session of archive/unarchive
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per distinct agent after Set deduplication, not one per chat; registered agent cardinality is small.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the session agent received the provider-specific archive notification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Calls are fire-and-forget relative to the state action. Existing worktree cleanup/recreation is also off the immediate action path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Moved chat chain/source-destination catalog size, or distinct agents represented in one session after deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Moves use the pre-existing global sequencer. Archive notifications may run concurrently, but aggregate concurrency is bounded by distinct registered agents rather than chat count.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The global chat-agent map is updated after durable writes and reused. Move config resolution groups applicable chats; no unbounded per-chat provider cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: serialization and Set-based deduplication are explicit, as are the durable move boundaries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider archive RPC duration varies, especially for Codex, but it is off the user-visible state-update critical path and distinct-agent count is low.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: newly required cross-agent lifecycle work is grouped, serialized where consistency requires it, and archive fan-out is deduplicated and asynchronous.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the 130-file inventory and relevant production/test diffs. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression met the reporting threshold. Recorded the PR's concrete fix for response-file-change subscription fan-out and its introducing commit.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
